name: Make charcoal
blurb: Wood heated without oxygen becomes nearly pure carbon: hotter-burning, smokeless fuel. A tin-can retort makes it a safe afternoon project.
gear: A metal tin with a small vent hole
A fire pit and long tongs
Gloves and eye protection, outdoors only
steps: Understand the principle: pyrolysis drives off water and volatiles, leaving carbon, and the exclusion of oxygen is what stops it becoming ash.
Pack a metal tin with dry hardwood pieces and make one small vent hole in the lid for gases to escape.
Build a good fire and place the tin in the coals.
Watch the vent: it will jet smoke and then flame as the wood gases burn off. When that stops, the process is finished.
Remove the tin with tongs, plug the vent hole, and let it cool completely sealed — opening it hot lets air in and burns your charcoal to ash.
Test the result: good charcoal is light, black through, rings when tapped, and lights easily.
tips: Do this outdoors only. The escaping gases include carbon monoxide and they are flammable.
Opening the tin while hot is the classic way to lose the whole batch to sudden combustion.
Cool it fully before storing — charcoal can reignite hours later.
proof: A batch of charcoal that lights readily and burns hot with almost no smoke.
